tooltip.hololith.table: A kinetic instrument for miniature 3D surface surveys.
tooltip.hololith.table.1: 3 × 3 footprint. Drive the underside of its center at 16+ RPM.
tooltip.hololith.table.2: Empty hand: panel. Wrench: rotate; sneak-wrench: area.
tooltip.hololith.table.3: Larger surveys/projections need more stress capacity. No power: no map.
tooltip.hololith.sensor: A movable survey location for linked tables.
tooltip.hololith.sensor.1: Use a Survey Card here, then on a table.
tooltip.hololith.sensor.2: Mount beneath a ship or on a Create contraption.
tooltip.hololith.sensor.3: Live updates need a loaded sensor. Offline sources show saved terrain.
tooltip.hololith.beacon: A remote survey location for your base or outpost.
tooltip.hololith.beacon.1: Use a Survey Card here, then on a distant table.
tooltip.hololith.beacon.2: Only saved terrain remains viewable while the beacon is unloaded.
tooltip.hololith.beacon.3: Does not load chunks. Breaking it requires a new card link.
tooltip.hololith.marker: A colored reference pin on a linked terrain survey.
tooltip.hololith.marker.1: Apply a recorded sensor card or a sneak-recorded table card.
tooltip.hololith.marker.2: Dye: color. Sneak-wrench: unlink. Empty hand: inspect link.
tooltip.hololith.marker.3: Works enclosed; must be loaded and inside the surveyed area.
tooltip.hololith.card.1: Use on a sensor or beacon, then a table or reference marker.
tooltip.hololith.card.2: Sneak-use a table to record its identity for marker links.
tooltip.hololith.card.3: Recording a new target replaces this card's previous target.
gui.hololith.source.tooltip: Use a Survey Card on a placed sensor or beacon, then this table. Offline sources show saved terrain until they load again.
message.hololith.sensor_required: Record a placed Local Survey Sensor or Remote Survey Beacon first.
tooltip.hololith.card.legacy_coordinates: Unsupported coordinate card — record a sensor or beacon to replace it.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_1: Place the table on a clear 3 x 3 floor. This raised bench has a 32 RPM drive connected underneath its center.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_2: The light projection preserves terrain height, water, trees and surface structures. This example surveys the tutorial model.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_3: Right-click the table to open its controls: survey area, source, rotation, magnification and vertical relief.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_4: Use a Create Wrench to turn the map by a quarter turn. The surveyed world stays in place.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_5: Sneak-use the Wrench to cycle 32, 64 and 128 block survey areas. Larger areas cover more ground; 128 uses coarser samples.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_6: Magnification enlarges the display and increases its stress load. Vertical relief changes elevation only. Neither loads extra terrain.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_1: A new table surveys around itself. This bench is powered from below; a Survey Card can point it at a different source.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_2: Use a Survey Card on a Local Survey Sensor to record its identity.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_3: Use that card on the table. It follows the sensor's current world position, including supported moving ships and contraptions.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_4: A Remote Survey Beacon links the same way. Leave one at a base to revisit that area's survey from another table.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_5: The controls switch between this table's position and its linked sensor or beacon. Survey targets must be physical instruments in the world.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_6: When a sensor or beacon goes offline, only its saved terrain remains while the table is powered. Live updates resume when it loads again; chunks are never force-loaded.
hololith.ponder.reference_markers.text_1: Sneak-use a Survey Card on the table to copy its identity for Reference Markers. The drive below powers this display.
hololith.ponder.reference_markers.text_2: Use the card on a placed marker. Its colored pin appears at the matching horizontal position in that table's known survey.
hololith.ponder.reference_markers.text_3: Use any of the sixteen dyes to recolor the physical marker and its pin. Choose your own colors for bases, routes and landmarks.
hololith.ponder.reference_markers.text_4: A sensor card can instead link markers to that sensor's survey group. Pins follow the map's rotation and scale; they are not entity trackers.
hololith.ponder.reference_markers.text_5: Sneak-use a Create Wrench on a marker to unlink it. The marker remains available to link again.
hololith.ponder.powering_table.text_1: Connect rotational power to the shaft socket underneath the center section. The motor here is a tutorial stand-in for a survival power source.
hololith.ponder.powering_table.text_2: The gears turn at 8 RPM, but the projection stays off. A Hololith needs at least 16 RPM in either direction.
hololith.ponder.powering_table.text_3: At 32 RPM the projection starts. At 100%% magnification, a 32-block survey uses 4 SU per RPM: 128 SU at this speed.
hololith.ponder.powering_table.text_4: A 64-block survey uses 8 SU per RPM at 100%% magnification: 256 SU at 32 RPM.
hololith.ponder.powering_table.text_5: A 128-block survey uses 16 SU per RPM at 100%% magnification: 512 SU at 32 RPM. Supply enough network capacity before expanding.
hololith.ponder.powering_table.text_6: Magnification multiplies stress by its square. At 150%%, the same 32-block survey needs 2.25 times the load: 9 SU per RPM, or 288 SU here.
hololith.ponder.powering_table.text_7: An overstressed survival network stops the machine and blanks the entire projection, including a cached map. Reduce the load or add capacity.
hololith.ponder.powering_table.text_8: Once sufficient power returns, the saved survey is visible again. Power loss does not erase the map or its links.
hololith.ponder.powering_table.text_9: A missing drive connection also turns the projection off. The table cannot display its saved map without rotational power.
hololith.ponder.powering_table.text_10: Reconnect the gear train and provide at least 16 RPM with enough stress capacity to resume surveying.
